overview: White prepares e4 with f3, aiming for a big pawn centre with c4, e4 and Nc3 and possibly a Blackmar-Diemer-like or Sämisch-style set-up. Black can strike at once with ...d5 or ...e5 or ...c5, or take on e4 and let White weaken the e1-h4 diagonal. I am unsure of the details and judge it from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Build a broad centre with e4, c4 and Nc3 behind the f3 pawn
Then develop Be3, Qd2 and aim at the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Strike at once with ...d5, ...e5 or ...c5 before e4 arrives
Exploit the weakened e1-h4 diagonal with ...Qh4+ and ...Ne4 ideas

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e4/f3 centre against a ...d5 or ...c5 counter

character.notes: White's slow but loosening f3 invites counterplay; not known for steadiness or mutual attack.

gambit.notes: Gambits like the Linder and Webster are sublines; no material in the main line.

soundness.notes: Loosening f3 is slightly inferior but not refuted.

structure.notes: Centre undecided; breaks like ...e5 or ...d5 are to come.

level.notes: Little theory but easy to misplay the weakened diagonal.

sublines_that_differ.name: Linder Counter Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a piece-for-pawn exchange sacrifice

sublines_that_differ.name: Webster Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: White gambits a pawn for central space

character.reason: Slightly loosening, neither especially solid nor forcing.

gambit.reason: No material is offered in the main line.

soundness.reason: Slightly inferior for White but not refuted.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided after f3.

level.reason: Few lines but the weakened diagonal makes it risky.

plans.reason: No clear named plan; White just builds the e4 centre.
